---
internalId: 583d9c88-b71c-4560-92ad-3e23d33bf1d0
---

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

Body: **Reviewer:** @jan-bogaerts

md²'s built-in model selectors and validation depended on configured model lists. A new model available through the installed client could therefore be missing from the application, as happened with GPT‑6.1 Sol. When providers introduce and retire models within a few months, those lists become a recurring compatibility and maintenance burden.

This PR moves Codex and Claude model selection to **dynamic binding through runtime catalog discovery**. The configured clients supply model identifiers, display names and supported capabilities; the selectors consume that metadata, and the desktop host validates the chosen model and settings before execution in the actual checkout. OpenAI Fast mode is exposed only when the effective provider and selected model advertise support.

**Model availability can now evolve independently of the md² release cycle.** An existing md² release containing this discovery path can use models introduced later without an immediate application upgrade or a change to `main` solely to add or remove model identifiers. Compatibility depends on the client continuing to expose a supported catalog and execution protocol; updating the provider client may still be necessary. This reduces urgent application maintenance while keeping newer models accessible to users of earlier md² releases that include this feature.

Saved selections remain explicit. A retired or unavailable model stays visible for correction, and execution is blocked when current capability validation fails. Discovery does not silently replace a user's selected model or automatically change their workflow to the newest model.

Implementation details:

- Discover Codex models through paginated `model/list` responses and effective provider configuration; read Claude's model catalog during initialization. Reuse the configured clients and their existing authentication. Catalog discovery submits no inference prompt.
- Cache catalogs by executable, configuration and checkout context, with bounded probes and explicit refresh. Resolve card/project discovery through the assigned branch and conflict discovery through its checkout path, keeping it aligned with execution after worktree cleanup. Use discovered model and reasoning capabilities across global defaults, action definitions and per-run controls. Custom provider profiles retain their configured model lists.
- Persist Provider default, Standard and Fast preferences. For OpenAI, apply the advertised Fast tier, including `priority`; explicit Standard sends `default`. Carry these settings through one-shot commands and streaming thread start, resume and turn requests, and distinguish requested settings from provider acknowledgements in history.

Validation:

- Merged main at `e74b8cec` without conflicts and committed the three-file checkout-discovery correction. The final head validated locally is `8720c3ae`.
- Desktop: 496 tests passed across 16 selected files. Frontend: 254 passed and 2 failed across 11 selected files. Both popup failures also reproduce on unchanged main at `e74b8cec`: `keeps usage absent from project-scoped agent popups` and `shows waiting action state through popup reopen, resume, and completion`. No additional failure names appeared in these checks.
- App and desktop lint, TypeScript compilation and production build passed. Regression coverage includes renamed and renumbered assignments, missing branches, and conflict checkout discovery. No full test suite was run.
- Earlier macOS packaging and native smoke on `464158ce` showed GPT‑6.1 Sol and supported OpenAI speed choices, with no Fast control for Claude. Native validation of the combined version, successful provider inference, real completed-conversation resume, Windows and connected remote hosts remain acceptance work. Catalog availability alone does not establish account access.

macOS and web users need a header that is as comfortable and usable as the Windows desktop experience. The previous layout reserved a fixed space on the right for every Electron window, even though macOS places its controls on the left. It also capped project titles despite available space and allowed search shortcuts to overflow in narrow layouts. This change adapts the header to the controls and space each user environment provides.

The scope is visual alignment and quality-of-life behavior. No kernel code, application core, agent execution, persistence, or domain logic is changed. Product changes are limited to header/search presentation and the Electron window-overlay height.

- Use the native window-control area for spacing: left on macOS, right on Windows, and no reserved area for macOS fullscreen or ordinary web deployments.
- Display as much of a long project title as the available gap allows, preserving 16 px of clearance from adjacent controls. Center fitting titles on the window and truncate constrained titles safely.
- Reduce search progressively from `Search cards…` to `Search`, then the complete keyboard shortcut, and finally a search icon. Keep the shortcut inside the field while it is visible.
- Keep pointer and keyboard access to search, preserve the entered query during responsive transitions, and retain the existing menu and Create controls at intermediate window widths.

Body: **Need**

Completed Claude turns can report too few tokens when subagents run and too much estimated cost when cumulative results are added repeatedly. This PR converts whole-tree provider snapshots into per-turn increments for both streaming and one-shot execution, so the existing conversation and project accumulators receive only newly accounted usage.

**Before and after**

Measured with in-process stream-json fixtures against upstream `e74b8cec` and this implementation; these are protocol regression examples, not live billing measurements.

| Input / trigger | Before this PR | After this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One turn: 120 main-agent tokens + 230 subagent tokens | 120 tokens recorded | 350 tokens recorded |
| Two results: whole-tree totals 350 then 470 tokens; cumulative costs $0.10 then $0.25 | 240 tokens and $0.35 accumulated | 470 tokens and $0.25 accumulated; second increment is 120 tokens / $0.15 |
| Resume with a saved 350-token / $0.10 baseline; next result totals 470 tokens / $0.25 | Adds the full $0.25 again | Adds 120 tokens / $0.15 |
| Replay the same result UUID | Adds another 120 tokens / $0.10 | Ignores the duplicate completion |

**Implementation route**

1. Decode validated `modelUsage` counters across every model, including subagents. Merge cache creation/read buckets and keep thinking inside output, matching the existing token schema. Retain the current per-turn result/message path when model counters are absent.
2. Share one stateful `ClaudeUsageTracker` across the two execution paths. Difference cumulative token/cost snapshots, scope baselines to the root provider session, handle conversation resets, ignore duplicate result UUIDs, and preserve the last valid baseline when a crash reports zeroed counters. Malformed or regressing counters fail clearly.
3. Persist the raw snapshot in `providerSessions[].usageBaseline`, separately from displayed conversation totals. Hydrate it on resume and save it together with accounted usage in the completed-turn conversation snapshot. The shared parser and TypeScript types retain this metadata.
4. Add regression coverage through both production protocol paths, completed-turn persistence, and conversation reload. Make two existing out-of-root path fixtures native to the host OS so the targeted tests also pass on macOS.

The counter scopes and reset behavior follow the [Claude cost-tracking documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#track-costs-in-streaming-input-mode) and [conversation-reset schema](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkconversationresetmessage). Resumed session totals follow the protocol documented for Claude Code v2.1.277 and later.

**Validation and limits**

- 243 desktop tests pass across nine selected files: accounting, decoders, protocols, runner state, conversation persistence, project totals, and usage metrics.
- 69 app tests pass across three selected files: conversation parsing, usage arithmetic, and project usage totals. Total: **312 passing targeted tests**, including 33 new regression cases.

Body: @jan-bogaerts — please review the before/after behavior comparison below; this draft is ready for testing.

Editing Markdown in Rich text could flatten explicit line breaks, lose reference definitions, or rewrite untouched source. Unsupported HTML also lacked a reliable way to recover the original document. This change preserves those constructs and adds Rich text/Source controls to the shared Markdown editor.

## Behavior

This comparison covers the shared document editor.

| Scenario | Before this PR | After this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Edit, save, and reopen text with an explicit hard break (two spaces or a backslash before a newline) | Rich export serialized the break as an ordinary newline, losing the explicit break on reopen. | The break remains explicit through edit/save/reopen. Ordinary soft newlines remain soft. |
| Open reference links/images such as `[one][doc]`, `[doc][]`, or `[doc]`, with a matching definition | Reference and definition nodes had no import visitors; valid reference-based Markdown could fail to load in Rich text. | Full, collapsed, and shortcut references resolve, including normalized labels and titles. Shared and unused definitions survive edits and reopen. |
| Change one link's destination when several occurrences share a definition | Reference-backed documents had no supported Rich text editing path. | Only the changed occurrence becomes an inline link; other references and the shared definition keep their destination. |
| Copy a reference link or image into another Markdown document | Reference-backed content had no supported Rich text import/export path for Markdown copy. | The selection includes its required definition, making the copied Markdown self-contained. |
| Open or flush a document without editing | The editor could replace original spelling or whitespace with its normalized serialization. | Opening and switching views without editing preserve the original source and clean state. Source edits save the typed text verbatim. |
| Inspect or edit Markdown source | Ordinary document editors had no Rich text/Source selector. | Document editors expose both views. Compact editors expose Source for recovery, and read-only previews allow inspection without editing. |
| Load raw HTML/comments, or paste unsupported content into Rich text | HTML-like nodes were forced into rich text; block HTML could fail import, and there was no reliable Source recovery path. | Loading recovers the original text in Source. An unsupported rich paste preserves the existing document and opens Source; paste again there to insert the raw content. |
| Insert text, paste, attach files, or use toolbar undo/redo while in Source | Shared insertion handlers targeted the rich editor; the shared toolbar had no Source undo/redo controls. | Insertion, paste, attachments, and Source undo/redo operate on the visible Source editor. Document switches and external replacements reset its text/history. |

Source undo belongs to the current Source session. Actual Source changes establish a new rich undo baseline so stale content cannot return; merely viewing Source preserves the existing rich undo history.

The conversion changes use MDXEditor's existing plugins and visitors. Literal command fields and historical diff views retain their existing behavior. Footnotes, Mermaid, math, repository-relative image loading, and a renderer replacement are outside this change.

## Validation

- 185 targeted tests passed across 12 files, including 30 regressions using installed MDXEditor/Lexical/CodeMirror, affected editor surfaces, document bindings, drafts, and history. The full suite was not run.
- `npm run lint-fix` and `npm run lint` passed with no lint warnings or errors.
- `npm run build` passed, including TypeScript checking. Vite reports its existing attachment dynamic-import and large-chunk warnings.
- Chromium smoke checks passed for a composed document containing references, hard breaks, tasks, a table, and a code fence; Source typing, undo/redo, insertion at the caret, and returning to Rich text were checked with no page errors.
- `git diff --check` passed.

The textarea test adapter disables duplicate native Lexical event dispatch, and local-search tests run independently so their MUI mock loads before the component. Parser recovery is tested against the real editor rather than a simulated error callback.

[Owner testing instructions and fixture](https://github.com/BinaryOutlook/md2/blob/146ca4bb105c90cab3739d7f6356096608d6dfd8/docs/markdown-editing-testing.md) are included in `docs/markdown-editing-testing.md`. This draft is ready for owner testing; acceptance and merge remain pending.

  - app/src/components/actions/run/popup/action_input_layout_store.test.ts
  - app/src/components/actions/run/popup/action_input_layout_store.ts

for command actions, the layout is incorrect: we show a splitter above the markdown input and the run history below the input.

the splitter should be between markdown editor and run history. it should be different from the agent-actions: it's position needs to be saved with a different config name.

also: do this properly: so no splitter in the same component as the markdown editor, but the command-action  component should contains input, splitter, history and agent-action component should contain chatlog-splitter-input. both components are allowed to have more, as architecture needs it, but this should be the basis

## Current state

- Bug remains valid. `ActionPopupContent` selects separate `CommandAction` and `AgentAction` components, but neither owns its splitter.
- Idle commands render `ActionPromptOwner`, then scheduling, status, and `ActionRunHistoryOwner`. `ActionPromptOwner` renders `ActionAgentPrompt`, which places splitter above input and owns resize state.
- Commands and agents share `md2.actionPromptHeight`. Agent questions use additional `md2.actionQuestionsBlockHeight`.
- Command input uses `MarkdownEditor` in plain-text, monospace mode; â€œmarkdown inputâ€ in original report means this editor, not Markdown formatting.
- During active command runs, command input disappears. A command can start an agent child: an agent step within that command run. `ActionAgentInteraction` then displays conversation and prompt.

## implementation details

- Move splitter rendering, pointer/keyboard handling, height limits, and persistence out of `ActionAgentPrompt`. Keep editor draft binding, preparation, shortcuts, and question behavior intact.
- `CommandAction` owns input, horizontal splitter, and run history in that order. â€œSplitterâ€ means draggable, keyboard-accessible separator that changes vertical space allocated to adjacent regions. Keep scheduling, status, and controls available without placing them between input and splitter.
- `AgentAction` owns conversation, splitter, and input in that order. Refactor `ActionAgentInteraction` so commands running agent children reuse agent layout without duplicating prompt or splitter.
- Shared call sites: `ActionPromptOwner` serves idle commands and `ActionAgentInteraction`; both lose embedded splitter. `ActionAgentPrompt` has only `ActionPromptOwner` as production caller. Commands receive new input/history layout; agents retain conversation/input layout and question resizing.
- Keep persistent layout state in service beside popup components. Use `EventTarget` notifications and `useSyncExternalStore` subscriptions at smallest affected region; editor must not own splitter state.
- Save command input height under `md2.commandActionInputHeight` through `applicationStorage`. Retain existing agent keys. New command setting starts from named default; do not copy shared agent height into it. Existing storage bridge accepts arbitrary keys; no desktop API change needed.
- Bound heights against available popup space after header and controls. Scroll input and history independently; recompute limits when popup size changes. Preserve empty-input collapse, read-only history, active-run input hiding, and agent questions.
- Add behavioral regression coverage for layout order, resize direction, persistence isolation, reopen, and agent-child transitions. Run affected tests and app linter; do not run full suite.

## acceptance criteria

- Idle command popup shows input, splitter, then run history; no splitter above command input.
- Dragging command splitter downward grows input; dragging upward shrinks it. Keyboard resize works and separator exposes accessible name and current value.
- Saved command height survives popup reopen and application restart. Resizing commands never changes agent heights, and resizing agents never changes command height.
- Agent popup retains conversation, splitter, then input. Pending questions and command-started agent children remain usable with one prompt and one relevant splitter.
- Empty input/history, long content, small popup, full-height mode, and popup resizing keep controls reachable and prevent negative region heights.
- Command text, draft retention, submission shortcuts, scheduling, read-only behavior, and active-run transitions remain unchanged.
- Editor component contains no splitter or splitter persistence. Action layouts own composition; layout service owns view state.

  - desktop/main.js

  - desktop/src/actions/action/action_scheduler_service.test.mjs
  - desktop/src/actions/schedule/scheduled_card_context.js
  - desktop/src/actions/schedule/scheduled_card_context.test.mjs
  - shared/action_worktree_context.d.mts
  - shared/action_worktree_context.mjs
after: 55b36bc4-6580-4a70-ad3d-0f413c2f37f8
---

## Bug

After PR [#24](https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2/pull/24), deleting or pruning an unrelated worktree can change an assigned card's displayed worktree number without changing its stored `worktree` field. The checkout and branch remain correctly assigned, but action filtering still uses the old number.

For example, a card assigned to worktree 2 moves to displayed position 1 after an earlier worktree is removed. An action filtered to worktree 1 does not match the card, while an action filtered to worktree 2 can match it even though the editor now labels 2 as another checkout.

## Current behavior and affected paths

* `app/src/data/action_context.ts` builds card and file action contexts from `card.header.worktreeValue`. `actionMatchesContext` compares `appliesTo.worktree` directly with that value.
* `app/src/components/actions/editor/action_filter_editor.tsx` builds worktree filter labels and values from current list positions.
* `desktop/src/actions/schedule/scheduled_card_context.js` also reads the stored card number for scheduled action contexts. PR #24 carries the expected branch for execution, but leaves this filter value unchanged.
* The worktree selector and project action context derive the current display number from the assigned branch. This issue concerns card and file action filtering, including scheduled card actions.

## Expected behavior

Actions shown and triggered for a card should agree with the worktree identified by the filter editor after list renumbering. A missing or invalid assignment should still fail safely. Resolving the filter semantics must not rewrite card metadata merely because Git reordered its list.

## Regression coverage

* With a card's stored number at 2 and its assigned branch now at position 1, verify which `appliesTo.worktree` value matches in the popup and in scheduled card action matching.
* Verify an action filtered to the number now occupied by another checkout does not match this card.
* Verify normal assignments and unavailable branches retain their existing behavior.

---
internalId: 583d9c88-b71c-4560-92ad-3e23d33bf1d0
---

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

Type: text
Text: Action completed.
Url: https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2/pull/28
Number: 28
State: open
Merged: false
Mergeable: false
Draft: false
Body: **Need**

Completed Claude turns can report too few tokens when subagents run and too much estimated cost when cumulative results are added repeatedly. This PR converts whole-tree provider snapshots into per-turn increments for both streaming and one-shot execution, so the existing conversation and project accumulators receive only newly accounted usage.

**Before and after**

Measured with in-process stream-json fixtures against upstream `e74b8cec` and this implementation; these are protocol regression examples, not live billing measurements.

| Input / trigger | Before this PR | After this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One turn: 120 main-agent tokens + 230 subagent tokens | 120 tokens recorded | 350 tokens recorded |
| Two results: whole-tree totals 350 then 470 tokens; cumulative costs $0.10 then $0.25 | 240 tokens and $0.35 accumulated | 470 tokens and $0.25 accumulated; second increment is 120 tokens / $0.15 |
| Resume with a saved 350-token / $0.10 baseline; next result totals 470 tokens / $0.25 | Adds the full $0.25 again | Adds 120 tokens / $0.15 |
| Replay the same result UUID | Adds another 120 tokens / $0.10 | Ignores the duplicate completion |

**Implementation route**

1. Decode validated `modelUsage` counters across every model, including subagents. Merge cache creation/read buckets and keep thinking inside output, matching the existing token schema. Retain the current per-turn result/message path when model counters are absent.
2. Share one stateful `ClaudeUsageTracker` across the two execution paths. Difference cumulative token/cost snapshots, scope baselines to the root provider session, handle conversation resets, ignore duplicate result UUIDs, and preserve the last valid baseline when a crash reports zeroed counters. Malformed or regressing counters fail clearly.
3. Persist the raw snapshot in `providerSessions[].usageBaseline`, separately from displayed conversation totals. Hydrate it on resume and save it together with accounted usage in the completed-turn conversation snapshot. The shared parser and TypeScript types retain this metadata.
4. Add regression coverage through both production protocol paths, completed-turn persistence, and conversation reload. Make two existing out-of-root path fixtures native to the host OS so the targeted tests also pass on macOS.

The counter scopes and reset behavior follow the [Claude cost-tracking documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#track-costs-in-streaming-input-mode) and [conversation-reset schema](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkconversationresetmessage). Resumed session totals follow the protocol documented for Claude Code v2.1.277 and later.

**Validation and limits**

- 243 desktop tests pass across nine selected files: accounting, decoders, protocols, runner state, conversation persistence, project totals, and usage metrics.
- 69 app tests pass across three selected files: conversation parsing, usage arithmetic, and project usage totals. Total: **312 passing targeted tests**, including 33 new regression cases.
- Desktop and app `npm run lint` pass; explicit lint of the changed shared parser passes; app `npm run typecheck` passes; `git diff --check` passes.
- The initial four accounting regressions failed against the old implementation. A separate before/after protocol probe confirms every comparison in the table.
- Existing resumed sessions without a saved raw baseline use their available main-agent turn counts for the first result and omit its unprovable cost increment. That result establishes the baseline for later whole-tree increments. Historical values are not reconstructed.
- Validation uses mocked provider/storage boundaries; no live Claude inference was run. Cross-file project-summary recovery remains outside this accounting normalization change.

Title: fix: correct Claude token and cost accounting

Body: @jan-bogaerts — please review the before/after behavior comparison below; this draft is ready for testing.

Editing Markdown in Rich text could flatten explicit line breaks, lose reference definitions, or rewrite untouched source. Unsupported HTML also lacked a reliable way to recover the original document. This change preserves those constructs and adds Rich text/Source controls to the shared Markdown editor.

## Behavior

This comparison covers the shared document editor.

| Scenario | Before this PR | After this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Edit, save, and reopen text with an explicit hard break (two spaces or a backslash before a newline) | Rich export serialized the break as an ordinary newline, losing the explicit break on reopen. | The break remains explicit through edit/save/reopen. Ordinary soft newlines remain soft. |
| Open reference links/images such as `[one][doc]`, `[doc][]`, or `[doc]`, with a matching definition | Reference and definition nodes had no import visitors; valid reference-based Markdown could fail to load in Rich text. | Full, collapsed, and shortcut references resolve, including normalized labels and titles. Shared and unused definitions survive edits and reopen. |
| Change one link's destination when several occurrences share a definition | Reference-backed documents had no supported Rich text editing path. | Only the changed occurrence becomes an inline link; other references and the shared definition keep their destination. |
| Copy a reference link or image into another Markdown document | Reference-backed content had no supported Rich text import/export path for Markdown copy. | The selection includes its required definition, making the copied Markdown self-contained. |
| Open or flush a document without editing | The editor could replace original spelling or whitespace with its normalized serialization. | Opening and switching views without editing preserve the original source and clean state. Source edits save the typed text verbatim. |
| Inspect or edit Markdown source | Ordinary document editors had no Rich text/Source selector. | Document editors expose both views. Compact editors expose Source for recovery, and read-only previews allow inspection without editing. |
| Load raw HTML/comments, or paste unsupported content into Rich text | HTML-like nodes were forced into rich text; block HTML could fail import, and there was no reliable Source recovery path. | Loading recovers the original text in Source. An unsupported rich paste preserves the existing document and opens Source; paste again there to insert the raw content. |
| Insert text, paste, attach files, or use toolbar undo/redo while in Source | Shared insertion handlers targeted the rich editor; the shared toolbar had no Source undo/redo controls. | Insertion, paste, attachments, and Source undo/redo operate on the visible Source editor. Document switches and external replacements reset its text/history. |

Source undo belongs to the current Source session. Actual Source changes establish a new rich undo baseline so stale content cannot return; merely viewing Source preserves the existing rich undo history.

The conversion changes use MDXEditor's existing plugins and visitors. Literal command fields and historical diff views retain their existing behavior. Footnotes, Mermaid, math, repository-relative image loading, and a renderer replacement are outside this change.

## Validation

- 185 targeted tests passed across 12 files, including 30 regressions using installed MDXEditor/Lexical/CodeMirror, affected editor surfaces, document bindings, drafts, and history. The full suite was not run.
- `npm run lint-fix` and `npm run lint` passed with no lint warnings or errors.
- `npm run build` passed, including TypeScript checking. Vite reports its existing attachment dynamic-import and large-chunk warnings.
- Chromium smoke checks passed for a composed document containing references, hard breaks, tasks, a table, and a code fence; Source typing, undo/redo, insertion at the caret, and returning to Rich text were checked with no page errors.
- `git diff --check` passed.

The textarea test adapter disables duplicate native Lexical event dispatch, and local-search tests run independently so their MUI mock loads before the component. Parser recovery is tested against the real editor rather than a simulated error callback.

[Owner testing instructions and fixture](https://github.com/BinaryOutlook/md2/blob/146ca4bb105c90cab3739d7f6356096608d6dfd8/docs/markdown-editing-testing.md) are included in `docs/markdown-editing-testing.md`. This draft is ready for owner testing; acceptance and merge remain pending.

Reviewed both. I found one issue in each:

- **[PR #29](https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2/pull/29) — Source edits can lose meaningful indentation.** Change `code` to `    code` in Source, then return to Rich text. It remains a paragraph instead of becoming a code block; the next rich edit removes the indentation. Reproduced with the real editor. The problem is in [the mode transition](https://github.com/BinaryOutlook/md2/blob/146ca4bb105c90cab3739d7f6356096608d6dfd8/app/src/components/editor/source/markdown_source_controller.ts#L119), which relies on MDXEditor’s trimmed comparison.

- **[PR #28](https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2/pull/28) — Resuming with older Claude versions can fail.** The saved baseline is always subtracted, but versions before 2.1.277 restart their totals at zero on resume. That produces negative usage and throws. [Anthropic documents this version boundary](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#accumulate-costs-across-multiple-calls). The app needs to enforce the minimum version.

**Validation:** 342 existing targeted tests passed, plus two additional review probes. Desktop and app lint passed. GitHub also reports merge conflicts for both PRs.

I’d request changes on both. No reviews were posted, and your working files are unchanged.

id: B_259
internalId: e461b100-4b8f-435e-9c0f-81426d7fdb47
title: Responsive search reopens after Escape and loses results on resize
status: new
---

Reported during review of [PR #27](https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2/pull/27), head `e1181650a`. Fix after the PR is merged.

## Search reopens after Escape

1. Use a window width where search shows the shortcut presentation.
2. Open search by clicking its launcher.
3. Press Escape.

The popover closes and immediately reopens. Closing should dismiss search and leave keyboard navigation usable.

`SearchControl` uses a MUI `Popover` that restores focus to the launcher on close. `SearchLauncher` opens search through its `onFocus` handler, so restored focus opens it again. A targeted regression probe reproduced the failure; disabling focus restoration in a temporary probe prevented reopening.

Affected files: `app/src/components/shell/search/search_control.tsx` and `search_launcher.tsx`.

## Resizing clears results and search options

1. Open inline search and enter a query that returns a result, such as `Beta` in the existing test fixture.
2. Resize until search changes to a popover presentation.

The query remains, but the matching results disappear. RegExp mode and the background-body/action options also reset. Resizing should preserve the active search, its options, and matching results in either direction.

`SearchControl` mounts `SearchPanel` in separate inline and popover branches. Changing presentation remounts the panel. Only the query survives in `SearchControl`; `SearchPanel` initializes empty results and default options and does not apply its initial query on mount.

Affected files: `app/src/components/shell/search/search_control.tsx` and `search_panel.tsx`.

## Regression coverage

- Open shortcut search, press Escape, and verify it stays closed without preventing later reopening.
- Search for a matching card and resize between inline and popover presentations; verify the query and result remain available.
- Enable RegExp mode and background-body/action options before resizing; verify their selections and search behavior survive.

Both reported failures were reproduced with temporary probes in `search_control.test.tsx`; the probes were removed after review. No fix is included in this report.

---
id: B_260
internalId: ef3c3a56-28a9-4ca5-9402-16972e140c01
title: Source indentation is lost when returning to Rich text
status: new
---

Reported during review of [PR #29](https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2/pull/29), head `146ca4bb105c90cab3739d7f6356096608d6dfd8`. Fix after the PR is merged.

## Reproduction

1. Open a Markdown document containing `code` as an ordinary paragraph.
2. Switch to Source and add four leading spaces: `    code`.
3. Switch back to Rich text.
4. Add another paragraph and save.

Rich text still shows an ordinary paragraph instead of an indented code block. The subsequent rich edit exports `code` without its indentation, losing the Source change.

Expected: returning to Rich text imports the indented code block. Later edits, saving, and reopening preserve its code-block meaning; serialization may use a fenced code block.

## Cause and affected code

`MarkdownSourceController.setMode()` detects the Source change using exact comparison, but publishes `viewMode$` to let MDXEditor import it. MDXEditor's `setMarkdown$` compares trimmed strings and skips importing when only outer whitespace differs. Here, the leading whitespace changes Markdown meaning, so the rich document remains stale and its next export overwrites the Source edit.

Affected files: `app/src/components/editor/source/markdown_source_controller.ts` and the shared `markdown_editor.tsx` integration. MDXEditor's comparison is in `@mdxeditor/editor/dist/plugins/core/index.js`.

The fix must import meaningful Source whitespace changes while preserving untouched source, clean-state behavior, and the existing undo baseline rules. Do not treat whitespace-only differences as equivalent without considering Markdown meaning.

## Regression coverage

- Change a paragraph into an indented code block in Source, return to Rich text, and verify code-block rendering.
- Make an unrelated rich edit, save, and reopen; verify the code-block meaning survives.
- Verify viewing Source without editing preserves the original text and rich undo history.

The indentation loss was reproduced with a temporary regression probe against the installed MDXEditor in `markdown_editor_reliability.real.test.tsx`. The probe was removed after review. No fix is included in this report.

---
internalId: 583d9c88-b71c-4560-92ad-3e23d33bf1d0
---

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

# App Style Guide â€” Kanban / MDÂ² (React + MUI)

How to build **any new component** so it matches the app. This is written for **Material UI v5+** components.

**The theme is the source of truth.** All color, radius, base typography, and spacing units live in the single `createTheme` (defined in `GUIDANCE.md` Â§1/Â§9). This guide does **not** define colors â€” it tells you **which theme value to use for which role**, and covers the things the theme can't encode: layout, spacing/margins, borders, elevation, and component conventions.

**The one rule that matters:** never write a raw hex, px radius, or magic color into a component. Read it from the theme (`theme.palette.*`, `theme.shape`, `theme.typography`, `theme.spacing`). If a component has a hardcoded hex in its `sx`/styled, it's wrong â€” that's exactly where the look drifts and where dark mode breaks.

---

## 1. How to consume the theme

- **Colors:** `sx={{ color: 'text.secondary', bgcolor: 'background.paper', borderColor: 'divider' }}` â€” MUI resolves dotted palette paths automatically in `sx`. In `styled`/JS use the callback form: `styled(Box)(({ theme }) => ({ color: theme.palette.text.secondary }))`.
- **Spacing:** use the 8px unit via the spacing scale â€” `sx={{ p: 2, gap: 1, mt: 1.5 }}` (`2` = 16px, `1` = 8px). Don't write `padding: '16px'`.
- **Radius:** `borderRadius: 1` (= `theme.shape.borderRadius` = 8) and multiples; for the fixed non-8 radii see Â§4.
- **Typography:** prefer `Typography variant=...` and `theme.typography.*` over ad-hoc `fontSize`.
- **Custom tokens:** roles the default MUI palette doesn't cover (column/track surfaces, the strong/hover border steps, `text-3/4`, section-header color, `primary-bg` tint, status colors) must exist in the theme under a namespace (e.g. `theme.palette.custom.*`) with light + dark values. Consume them the same way â€” `bgcolor: 'custom.column'`. **Never inline their hex.** If a needed token doesn't exist yet, add it to the theme, don't hardcode it in the component.

---

## 2. Role â†’ theme slot

Pick the slot by the element's **role**, not by how it looks in one mode:

| Role | Theme slot |
|---|---|
| App background; tinted footer/action bars | `background.default` |
| Column & sidebar surface | `custom.column` |
| Segmented-control / toolbar track, hover fill | `custom.track` |
| Card, dialog, popup, input surface | `background.paper` |
| Hairlines, resting borders | `divider` |
| Input borders, vertical separators | `custom.borderStrong` |
| Border on hover | `custom.borderHover` |
| Titles, values, headings | `text.primary` |
| Body copy, field labels | `text.secondary` |
| Meta, captions, resting icons | `custom.text3` |
| Muted / placeholder / disabled | `custom.text4` |
| Uppercase section/column headers | `custom.colHead` |
| The one CTA, selection, focus, links, icon-hover | `primary.main` |
| Contained-button hover | `primary.dark` |
| Selected/tinted bg, focus ring, ID-chip bg | `custom.primaryBg` |
| Text/icon on a primary fill | `primary.contrastText` |
| Active / saved / online dot | `success.main` |
| Destructive action | `error.main` |
| Status swatch dots & ID-chip tints (decorative only) | `custom.status.*` |

Rules: **one** `primary` per surface (the CTA/selection accent) â€” everything else is `text-*`/`divider`. Status colors are **decoration only** (dots, chip tints), never interactive color. Dark-mode brightness/tinting is handled inside the theme's two palettes, so a correctly-sloted component needs zero per-mode code.

---

## 3. Layout

- **Full-height app:** column flex â€” menu row / ribbon / content (`flex: 1; minHeight: 0`) / status bar. Fixed bands `flexShrink: 0`.
- **Board:** horizontal-scroll flex row, `gap: 2` (16px), page padding `p: 2.5` (20px); columns `width: 296, flexShrink: 0`, internal column flex `gap: 1`.
- **List view:** two-pane flex row filling the space between ribbon and status bar â€” sidebar `width: 280, flexShrink: 0`, editor p

can the claude cli work with other api endpoints then those of enthropic

**Yes.** Claude Code CLI can use other endpoints. Point it there with env vars.

**1. Built-in cloud providers (officially supported)**
- AWS Bedrock: `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1`, plus your AWS credentials and region
- Google Vertex AI: `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1`, plus `ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_PROJECT_ID` and `CLOUD_ML_REGION`
- Microsoft Foundry: `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY=1`

**2. Custom endpoint, gateway or proxy**
- `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`: URL of the endpoint
- `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (sent as a Bearer token) or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
- `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL`: map model names to the ones the endpoint knows

The endpoint must speak the **Anthropic Messages API format**:
- **Corporate gateways** like LiteLLM work, and are documented officially.
- **Non-Anthropic models** (OpenAI, Gemini, local Ollama and so on) need a translating proxy, such as LiteLLM or claude-code-router. Some vendors also offer Anthropic-compatible endpoints directly, for example DeepSeek, Kimi/Moonshot and GLM/Zhipu.
- **Caveat:** non-Claude models aren't officially supported. Tool use, caching, thinking and similar features may break or work poorly.

**Example (PowerShell, current session only):**
```powershell
$env:ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL = "http://localhost:4000"
$env:ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN = "sk-..."
$env:ANTHROPIC_MODEL = "my-model"
claude
```

**To make it persistent:** put the same keys in the `"env"` block of `~/.claude/settings.json`.

---

---
internalId: 583d9c88-b71c-4560-92ad-3e23d33bf1d0
---

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

entries.content:
This is a regression in the new **model-discovery check**.

During integration, Git first rebases the worktree. If that rebase hits conflicts, the checkout has a **detached HEAD**, so its refreshed worktree record has `branch: null`. [The popup check](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/hooks/use_action_catalog_project.ts:18) interprets that missing branch as “Merge conflict checkout is unavailable” and disables sending prompts.

The requirement was introduced in commit `464158ce0` (“discover provider models and support OpenAI Fast mode”). Commit `8720c3aef` later changed the lookup to use the checkout path, but retained the incorrect branch requirement. Existing tests only cover conflict checkouts with a named branch.

The fix is to:

- Expose the conflict checkout’s captured branch in `MergeConflictSession`, using the desktop session’s `projectBranch` or `worktreeBranch`.
- Use that session branch for model discovery instead of the refreshed worktree record.
- Add a regression test for a paused rebase whose worktree record has `branch: null`.

The backend [already permits detached HEAD during an active conflict rebase](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/git/worktree_service.js:606) and uses the captured branch to run the agent. The popup needs to follow the same logic.

No files changed.
fix it
I’ll use the conflict session’s captured branch in the popup, add a regression test for detached HEAD, and run the affected tests and linters.

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

The desktop already stores the original branch and accepts detached HEAD during an active conflict rebase. I’ll expose that branch in the public session and use it for popup model discovery.

The session projection has two call sites—initial load and updates—and both need the branch field. Card and project action checkout selection will keep its current behavior.

Body: **Need**

Completed Claude turns can report too few tokens when subagents run and too much estimated cost when cumulative results are added repeatedly. This PR converts whole-tree provider snapshots into per-turn increments for both streaming and one-shot execution, so the existing conversation and project accumulators receive only newly accounted usage.

**Before and after**

Measured with in-process stream-json fixtures against upstream `e74b8cec` and this implementation; these are protocol regression examples, not live billing measurements.

| Input / trigger | Before this PR | After this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One turn: 120 main-agent tokens + 230 subagent tokens | 120 tokens recorded | 350 tokens recorded |
| Two results: whole-tree totals 350 then 470 tokens; cumulative costs $0.10 then $0.25 | 240 tokens and $0.35 accumulated | 470 tokens and $0.25 accumulated; second increment is 120 tokens / $0.15 |
| Resume with a saved 350-token / $0.10 baseline; next result totals 470 tokens / $0.25 | Adds the full $0.25 again | Adds 120 tokens / $0.15 |
| Replay the same result UUID | Adds another 120 tokens / $0.10 | Ignores the duplicate completion |

**Implementation route**

1. Decode validated `modelUsage` counters across every model, including subagents. Merge cache creation/read buckets and keep thinking inside output, matching the existing token schema. Retain the current per-turn result/message path when model counters are absent.
2. Share one stateful `ClaudeUsageTracker` across the two execution paths. Difference cumulative token/cost snapshots, scope baselines to the root provider session, handle conversation resets, ignore duplicate result UUIDs, and preserve the last valid baseline when a crash reports zeroed counters. Malformed or regressing counters fail clearly.
3. Persist the raw snapshot in `providerSessions[].usageBaseline`, separately from displayed conversation totals. Hydrate it on resume and save it together with accounted usage in the completed-turn conversation snapshot. The shared parser and TypeScript types retain this metadata.
4. Add regression coverage through both production protocol paths, completed-turn persistence, conversation reload, and Codex run setup. The streaming adapter retains Codex model, effort, and service-tier settings alongside the Claude accounting tracker. Make two existing out-of-root path fixtures native to the host OS so the targeted tests also pass on macOS.

The counter scopes and reset behavior follow the [Claude cost-tracking documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking#track-costs-in-streaming-input-mode) and [conversation-reset schema](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdkconversationresetmessage). Resumed session totals follow the protocol documented for Claude Code v2.1.277 and later.

**Validation and limits**

- 249 desktop tests pass across ten selected files: accounting, decoders, protocols, run setup, runner state, conversation persistence, project totals, and usage metrics. The two new Codex run-setup cases also pass independently and detect a dropped execution-settings argument.
- 69 app tests pass across three selected files: conversation parsing, usage arithmetic, and project usage totals. Total: **318 passing targeted tests**, including 35 new regression cases.
- Desktop and app `npm run lint` pass; explicit lint of the changed shared parser passes; app `npm run typecheck` passes; `git diff --check` passes.
- The initial four accounting regressions failed against the old implementation. A separate before/after protocol probe confirms every comparison in the table.
- Existing resumed sessions without a saved raw baseline use their available main-agent turn counts for the first result and omit its unprovable cost increment. That result establishes the baseline for later whole-tree increments. Historical values are not reconstructed.
- Validation uses mocked provider/storage boundaries; no live Claude inference was run. Cross-file project-summary recovery remains outside this accounting normalization change.
